column1: # Where each woven French verb form in lex-fr.tsv was read.
# A verb row weaves its second form under an English -ing, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. French weaves the present
# participle, which English Wiktionary's conjugation table prints in a row
# it calls "present participle or gerund", the gérondif being that form
# after en. On 2026-10-08 every woven French form was read in that row of
# the table on English Wiktionary's French entry for its verb, rendered as
# a reader sees it, because a verb's headword line prints none of its
# forms. All 79 are the form their verb's table prints, and none was
# quote is the row's label and its cell, as printed. asseoir's cell prints
# two forms, "assoyant or asseyant", and the pack weaves the second.
# Whether that form answers to every English -ing it is woven under — the
# progressive's participle, or a gerund used as a noun, "reading is fun" —
# is a call about the language rather than a lookup, written up in TODO.md
# tests/tools/verb-forms.test.ts requires every verb lex-fr.tsv weaves in
# a second form to have a line here with that form, citing the verb's own
# entry, its quote printing the form in the "present participle or gerund" cell, and fails on a

column5: present participle or gerund assoyant or asseyant
